articles.title: How I drew all 11,064 bird species with Claude Code and Codex, and why the reviewer mattered more than the artist
articles.excerpt: I drew a sticker for every living bird species on Earth. All 11,064 of them, every species in the IOC World Bird List v15.2, and I've put them on GitHub along with structured data for each species: na…
articles.body: I drew a sticker for every living bird species on Earth. All 11,064 of them, every species in the IOC World Bird List v15.2, and I've put them on GitHub along with structured data for each species: names in up to 43 languages, Wikidata / eBird / GBIF / iNaturalist IDs, range, subspecies, body measurements and IUCN status. Repo: https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-bird-sticker Two things up front. First, I don't write code. Everything here was built by AI agents I directed: Claude Code as the orchestrator, Codex (with GPT-image) as the illustrator. Second, these are AI illustrations, not hand-painted, and not all of them are good. 7,676 meet the quality bar we set; 3,388 don't, and the data says which. I'd rather you hear that from me.
articles.author: 花叔 Huashu

articles.title: I remade my mobile game's trailer. Gameplay in a frame, text outside it.
articles.excerpt: This week I took every promo clip for my games off YouTube. They weren't broken. They were just too much: gameplay stretched edge to edge, big captions sitting on top of it, cuts so fast you couldn't…
articles.body: This week I took every promo clip for my games off YouTube. They weren't broken. They were just too much: gameplay stretched edge to edge, big captions sitting on top of it, cuts so fast you couldn't follow the shot. My game is a puzzle game about one careful shot, and the clips felt like the opposite of that. So I rebuilt the trailer for Bloop: One Bullet Ricochet, one game at a time, with a few rules I'm keeping from now on. Rule 1: the gameplay gets a frame, the text stays out of it The real game capture sits in the centre in a rounded card with a glowing border. Every headline lives in a band above the card, never on top of the gameplay. The card never moves out of place, only what's inside it changes, so the eye always knows where to look. The band isn't random.
articles.author: Rahim Khan

Behind that simple screen is a change we've wanted to make for a while: using Web-Engine Sentry, our own bot-protection service, to stop spam and make sign-in faster for real people. Like any site with public sign-up forms, it attracts bots.

articles.title: Network Timeout Diagnosis: Tracing Failure Alert APIs Across Media Tenant Cohorts
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: A timeout alert says that a request exceeded a deadline. It does not say where the time went. To identify the cause, record one request identifier and separate DNS, connection, TLS, request wri…
articles.body: TL;DR: A timeout alert says that a request exceeded a deadline. It does not say where the time went. To identify the cause, record one request identifier and separate DNS, connection, TLS, request write, time to first byte, and response-body timing. Add tenant cohort, experiment variant, destination, retry attempt, and deadline as structured fields. Then compare distributions by cohort, not just a single global error rate. The operational constraint is signal quality. In a media experiment, a noisy timeout alert can make one tenant cohort look unhealthy when the real problem is a shared egress path or an overloaded downstream. My default is to preserve the request's timing phases and correlate the client log with a trace or span.
articles.author: KendrickBerg5327

articles.title: # OpenTrace: Turn noisy logs into your next best move
articles.excerpt: What I built OpenTrace is a local-first debugging assistant for developers. A user pastes Live demo: https://opentrace-ai-debugger.onrender.com Source code: https://github.com/samainakhatun115-cpu/ope…
articles.body: What I built OpenTrace is a local-first debugging assistant for developers. A user pastes an error, stack trace, or service log and receives a structured report with a summary, severity, evidence, likely cause, safe next actions, and questions that would improve the diagnosis. Live demo: https://opentrace-ai-debugger.onrender.com Source code: https://github.com/samainakhatun115-cpu/opentrace-ai-debugger Why this problem Logs are often technically detailed but operationally unclear. The final error message may hide the first useful signal, and a generic chatbot can present a guess as a fact. OpenTrace makes the distinction visible: evidence is shown separately from hypotheses, and every response includes safe next steps rather than destructive commands.
articles.author: Samaina Khatun

articles.title: Enrich a list of company domains with emails, socials and tech stack (Python)
articles.excerpt: You have a column of company domains, from a CRM export, a conference attendee list, or a list of companies that are hiring. You want a few useful fields for each one: the real company name, a one-lin…
articles.body: You have a column of company domains, from a CRM export, a conference attendee list, or a list of companies that are hiring. You want a few useful fields for each one: the real company name, a one-line description, a contact email, LinkedIn and other social profiles, and where their careers page is. Paid enrichment APIs exist, but much of this is published on the company's own website, often in machine-readable form. This post shows how to get it yourself, what makes it harder than it looks, and a hosted option. Where the data lives <title> and <meta name="description"> . The tagline, almost always present. schema.org JSON-LD. Many sites embed an Organization block with name , logo , address , foundingDate and sameAs (their social profiles).

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower isn't much to look at. That's why I love it
articles.excerpt: The Taurids produce only a handful of meteors an hour. That sounds disappointing, but I've learned that expecting almost nothing can make this one of the most enjoyable meteor showers of the year.
articles.body: I used to make a basic mistake with meteor showers — I treated the zenith hourly rate (ZHR) like a timetable. If a shower were advertised at 20 meteors per hour, I'd go outside expecting something roughly every three minutes. After 10 quiet minutes, I'd start wondering what I was doing wrong. After half an hour, I'd start to doubt the whole idea of meteor showers . The Northern and Southern Taurids cured me of all that. Two linked meteor showers that peak around Nov. 4-5 and Nov. 11-12 this year, they each manage only about five meteors per hour under ideal conditions. In reality, you may see fewer. You may spend a long time seeing none. So what's the point?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
articles.excerpt: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11 , the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker . During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

articles.title: Watch Virgin Galactic's new 'Delta-class' space plane take to the skies for the 1st time (video)
articles.excerpt: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane, the newly named Apeiron, lifted off for the first time on Thursday (Oct. 29) —beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft.
articles.body: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico. "Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday . "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived." Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron, takes to the skies for the first time on Oct. 28, 2026, beneath the wings of its carrier plane, VMS Eve.
